A seat arrives with a hull and a thread of scheduled position pings. The applicant files a limited-entry permit, a hull number and a vessel monitoring unit. The node reads the satellite feed and requires the track to cross the epoch's grid cell near the tide's zenith. One transmitter, one hull, one seat, rechecked each season against the registry.

Fifty clones need fifty hulls: permit 85,000 dollars, survey 4,000, transponder 3,200 plus 400 airtime, near 4.6 million before a net leaves the dock.

A vessel occupies one stretch of ocean at a time, and the satellite sees which.
